simple.meaning: בְּקַר (bᵉqar) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “inquire, make search.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Ezra, beginning at Ezra 4:15. Its contexts include family, Torah, kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בְּקַר (H1240).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: בְּקַר (bᵉqar) / H1240 is traced through Ezra 4:15, Ezra 4:19, Ezra 5:17, Ezra 6:1 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H1240. beqar [ בְּקַר ] verb Pa`el inquire, seek (only Ezra) ( ᵑ7 Syriac; see Biblical Hebrew); — Perfect 3masculine plural בַּקַּ֫רוּ Dan 4:19 ; 6:1 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יְבַקַּר 4:15 ; Infinitive לְבַקָּרָה 7:14 ; — 1 inquire , with עַל (of thing) concerning 7:14 ; with subject indefinite, = passive, 4:19 search was made , so 6:1 ; 4:15 . Hithpa. Imperfect 3masculine singular יִתְבַּקַּר Dan 5:17 , impersonal, let search be made.

occurrences.englishText: that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. You will see in the book of the records, and know that this city is a rebellious city, and hurtful to kings and provinces, and that they have started rebellions within it in the past. That is why this city was destroyed.
I decreed, and search has been made, and it was found that this city has made insurrection against kings in the past, and that rebellion and revolts have been made in it.

Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the king’s treasure house, which is there at Babylon, whether it is so, that a decree was made of Cyrus the king to build this house of God at Jerusalem; and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.”
Then Darius the king made a decree, and the house of the archives, where the treasures were laid up in Babylon, was searched.
Because you are sent by the king and his seven counselors, to inquire concerning Judah and Jerusalem, according to the law of your God which is in your hand,
